validity.recommendation: no action — real, correctly specified trunk; add the sourced refs below
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/SPEC confirmed by three independent, non-GEM sources that name this exact pipeline (Раздельная-Измаил / Rozdilna-Izmail), all consistent with GEM's recorded values: (1) neftegaz.ru, 2015-07-28, quoting an Ukrtransgaz press statement about a joint capital-repair meeting with Moldovagaz: states the pipeline's 'протяженность 230 км и проектную пропускную мощность 7,3 млрд м3/год' (length 230 km, design capacity 7.3 bcm/y) — matches GEM's LengthKnown=230.00 km and Capacity=7.30 bcm/y exactly. Also gives repair history (17.2 km resurfaced 2011, 13 km 2012) and names the then-operator as a branch of UMG 'Prykarpattransgaz' (pre-2020, i.e. before the 2020 Ukrtransgaz/TSOU unbundling — not evidence about the current operator). (2) Moldovatransgaz's own asset list (moldovatransgaz.md/ru/news/54, archived) lists 'Раздельная-Измаил (РИ)' among the 8 trunk lines it operates on Moldovan territory: diameter 820 mm, capacity 7.3 bcm/y (matches GEM's Diameter=820mm exactly), oriented toward the Balkan countries, with a MOLDOVAN-TERRITORY length of 92.24 km — a subset of, and fully consistent with, the 230 km Ukraine-to-Ukraine total (Ukraine -> Moldova -> Ukraine transit corridor). (3) pridnestrovie-daily.net (Transnistrian outlet, archived), 2015-11-18: reports that Tiraspoltransgaz-Pridnestrovie completed capital repair of a 3 km section (km 116.9-119.9) of the 'магистральный газопровод Раздельная-Измаил' in Slobodzeya district, and states the pipeline 'был введен в эксплуатацию в 1975 году' (commissioned in 1975) — matches GEM's StartYear1=1975 exactly — and that 34 km of the line lies on PMR (Transnistrian) territory. (4) eadaily.com, 2019-08-20, quoting a further Ukrtransgaz statement: names 'Раздельная-Измаил' and 'Шебелинка-Днепропетровск-Кривой Рог-Измаил' as the two trunk lines Ukraine planned to use for reverse-flow gas imports from the Romanian Isaccea-1/Orlivka interconnection point starting Jan 2020 — confirms the pipeline is a real, currently-relevant asset used for a genuine, non-transit purpose (matches scope guidance point 3: transit ending does not mean the line is out of service). GEM's Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, StartLocation=Rozdilna/EndLocation=Izmail all check out. FLAG (see separate concern entries below): (a) an ownership/attribution question about the 100%-TSOU owner record given this line demonstrably transits Moldovan and Transnistrian territory operated by other entities, and (b) a possible spec overlap with P0784 worth a cluster-level look.

validity.recommendation: verify Owner split — do not treat TSOU as the sole operator; consider a Ukraine/Moldova(/PMR) owner split or a ResearcherNotes caveat
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records Owner1 = 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' at 100%. But the same-named pipeline is independently confirmed (moldovatransgaz.md) to have a ~92.24 km section that Moldovatransgaz — a legally separate Moldovan entity, not TSOU — owns/operates on Moldovan territory, plus a further 34 km inside Transnistria (PMR) operated by yet another distinct entity, 'Тираспольтрансгаз-Приднестровье' (per pridnestrovie-daily.net, which performed the PMR-side capital repairs itself, not TSOU or its predecessor Ukrtransgaz). Out of the 230 km total, well over 100 km therefore sits under non-Ukrainian, non-TSOU operational control. This is the same pattern the country scope-guidance calls out for Gazprom/cross-border rows: 'the correct reading is a split ... establish this once and apply it consistently.' I could not find a source stating TSOU owns 100% of this specific line, and the primary sources instead point to a genuine three-jurisdiction split (Ukraine/TSOU, Moldova/Moldovatransgaz, PMR/Tiraspoltransgaz-Pridnestrovie). Recommend Update review the Owner field rather than treating the existing 100% TSOU value as sourced by the tsoua.com citation staged below (that source only establishes TSOU's country-wide GTS-operator role since 2020-01-01, not ownership of this specific transit corridor's Moldovan/PMR sections).

validity.recommendation: cluster-level adjudication vs P0784 (do not merge/change unilaterally)
validity.researcher_notes: Per the Izmail-corridor cluster note (P0784/P0786/P0787): Moldovatransgaz's own asset list gives its transiting section of the line it calls 'Шебелинка-Днепропетровск-Кривой Рог-Измаил (ШДКРИ)' — clearly the same name family as GEM's P0784 'Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Rozdilna-Izmail' — a diameter of 820 mm and a capacity of 7.3 bcm/y, i.e. IDENTICAL specs to P0787's Rozdilna-Izmail line (also 820 mm / 7.3 bcm/y) in the Moldovan segment (91.817 km, almost the same as P0787's Moldovan-segment 92.24 km). GEM's own P0784 record instead carries 1200 mm / 24 bcm/y and a total length of only 164 km — specs that belong to the big Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih trunk further upstream, not to the Rozdilna-Izmail tail leg that actually crosses into Moldova/Izmail. This is consistent with the two GEM rows sharing a common physical tail segment near Izmail (i.e., a possible partial double-count between P0787 and P0784), and separately confirms the standing note that P0784's 164 km total is implausible for a route spanning Shebelinka to Izmail. By contrast, P0786 'Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail' matches a DIFFERENT Moldovatransgaz line item ('Ananьев-Тирасполь-Измаил (АТИ)', 1220 mm / 20 bcm/y) and does not appear to overlap with P0787. Flagging for cluster adjudication, not resolving here — P0784 is outside this row's scope.

fills.researcher_notes: Ukrtransgaz's own 2015 statement (via neftegaz.ru) states the МГП Раздельная-Измаил has 'протяженность 230 км' — exact match. Consistent with (not contradicted by) Moldovatransgaz's 92.24 km figure for the Moldovan-territory portion only.
Moldovatransgaz's own network page lists 'Раздельная-Измаил (РИ)' as диаметром 820 мм — exact match to GEM's 820 mm. Only one explicit-diameter source found; no contradicting figure anywhere.

Two independent legal entities both state 7.3 bcm/y design capacity for this exact pipeline: Ukrtransgaz (2015, via neftegaz.ru: 'проектную пропускную мощность 7,3 млрд м3/год') and Moldovatransgaz (asset list: 'пропускной способностью 7,3 млрд м3 в год'). Exact match to GEM's 7.30 bcm/y.

pridnestrovie-daily.net (2015-11-18, reporting on Tiraspoltransgaz-Pridnestrovie's completed repair of the PMR section) states the Rozdilna-Izmail trunk 'был введен в эксплуатацию в 1975 году' — exact match to GEM's StartYear1=1975. Single source (PMR outlet reporting a routine infrastructure fact, not a contested political claim); no contradicting date found anywhere.

Multiple independent sources consistently name the pipeline's endpoints as Rozdilna (Раздельная, Odesa Oblast) and Izmail (Измаил, Odesa Oblast, on the Danube). Note the corridor transits Moldovan (~92 km, Moldovatransgaz) and Transnistrian (~34 km, PMR) territory between the two Ukrainian endpoints — a routing detail worth a ResearcherNotes mention, though it does not change the recorded Start/End locations (both are correctly in Ukraine).
Both sources describe it as a 'газопровод' / 'магистральный газопровод' transporting 'природного газа' (natural gas) — confirms Fuel=Gas.

2019 Ukrtransgaz statement (quoted by eadaily.com, an independent outlet) names Rozdilna-Izmail as one of the two lines slated to carry reverse-flow gas imports from Romania starting Jan 2020 — confirms the line was in active service as of 2019/2020. No dated post-2020 source found showing it out of service; per country scope guidance, the 2025 end of Russian transit is not evidence of retirement absent line-specific evidence, which I did not find. Only one directly dated confirmation of ongoing operation, hence tier=medium rather than high — a fresher (2023-2026) confirmation would strengthen this.

summary: P0787 (Rozdilna-Izmail, 230 km/820mm/7.3 bcm/y, 1975) confirmed real and correctly specified by 3+ independent Russian/Moldovan/Transnistrian-language sources (Ukrtransgaz via neftegaz.ru + eadaily.com, Moldovatransgaz's own asset list, pridnestrovie-daily.net); staged refs for Length/Diameter/Capacity/Start/Location/Fuel/Status. Two concerns flagged, not resolved: (1) attribution — 100% TSOU ownership looks incomplete given confirmed Moldovan/Transnistrian transiting sections operated by other entities; Owner fill left UNRESOLVED; (2) duplicate/cluster — P0784's recorded 1200mm/24bcm/164km specs conflict with Moldovatransgaz's data on the same-named corridor's Izmail-bound tail (820mm/7.3bcm, matching P0787), suggesting a possible partial overlap between P0784 and P0787 worth cluster-level adjudication.
